```lean4
import Mathlib.Tactic

open Nat

theorem rmo_2001_2 (p q : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hq : Nat.Prime q) :
  (∃ m : ℕ, p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 = m^2) ↔
    (p = q ∨ (p = 3 ∧ q = 11) ∨ (p = 11 ∧ q = 3)) := by
  constructor
  · -- Forward direction: if there exists m, then one of the conditions holds
    intro h
    rcases h with ⟨m, hm⟩
    have h₁ : p ≤ m := by
      nlinarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, Nat.Prime.two_le hq]
    have h₂ : q ≤ m := by
      nlinarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, Nat.Prime.two_le hq]
    
    -- Consider the cases
    by_cases hpq : p = q
    · exact Or.inl hpq
    · -- p ≠ q, so we need p = 3 ∧ q = 11 or p = 11 ∧ q = 3
      have h₃ : p = 3 ∧ q = 11 ∨ p = 11 ∧ q = 3 := by
        by_contra! h₄
        -- We'll show that if p ≠ q and not (3,11) or (11,3), then no solution exists
        have h₅ : p ≠ 3 ∨ q ≠ 11 := by tauto
        have h₆ : p ≠ 11 ∨ q ≠ 3 := by tauto
        
        -- Use omega to derive contradiction from the equation
        have h₇ : p < m := by
          contrapose! h₅
          simp_all [pow_two]
          nlinarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, Nat.Prime.two_le hq]
        
        have h₈ : q < m := by
          contrapose! h₆
          simp_all [pow_two]
          nlinarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, Nat.Prime.two_le hq]
        
        -- Analyze bounds more carefully
        have h₉ : m^2 = p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 := by linarith
        
        -- Show that for p ≠ q and not (3,11)/(11,3), this leads to contradiction
        have h₁₀ : False := by
          -- Case analysis based on ordering
          cases' lt_or_gt_of_ne hpq with hpq hpq
          · -- p < q
            have h₁₁ : p ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le hp
            have h₁₂ : q ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le hq
            
            -- Since p < q and both are primes, check possible values
            interval_cases p <;> interval_cases q <;> norm_num at hm ⊢ <;> 
              (try omega) <;> (try {
                ring_nf at hm
                omega
              })
          · -- p > q  
            have h₁₁ : p ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le hp
            have h₁₂ : q ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le hq
            
            -- Since p > q and both are primes
            cases' le_total p q with h₁₁ h₁₁
            · exfalso; linarith
            · -- p > q
              have h₁₃ : q < p := by omega
              cases' lt_or_eq_of_le h₁₃ with h₁₄ h₁₄
              · -- q < p
                -- Similar analysis as above but with roles reversed
                interval_cases q <;> interval_cases p <;> norm_num at hm ⊢ <;> 
                  (try omega) <;> (try {
                    ring_nf at hm
                    omega
                  })
              · exfalso; linarith
        exact absurd h₁₀ (by simp)
      cases' h₃ with h₃ h₃
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inl h₃)
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inr h₃)
  · -- Backward direction: if one of the conditions holds, then there exists m
    intro h
    cases' h with h h
    · -- Case p = q
      rcases h with rfl
      refine' ⟨3 * p, _⟩
      simp [pow_two, mul_add, add_mul, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc]
      ring
    · -- Case p = 3 ∧ q = 11

    · -- Case p = 11 ∧ q = 3
```

$p^2 + 7pq + q^2 = m^2$

Since we're looking at primes, let's consider different cases.

Case 1: $p = q$
Then $p^2 + 7p^2 + p^2 = 9p^2 = (3p)^2$, which is always a perfect square.
So any prime $p$ with $q = p$ works.

Case 2: $p \neq q$
Without loss of generality, assume $p < q$.

$p^2 + 7pq + q^2 = m^2$
$(p+q)^2 + 5pq = m^2$
$m^2 - (p+q)^2 = 5pq$

```lean
import Mathlib

open Nat

-- Helper: When p = q, the expression equals (3p)²
lemma eq_self_sq (p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) :
  ∃ m : ℕ, p^2 + 7*p*p + p^2 = m^2 := by
  use 3 * p
  simp [pow_two, mul_assoc, mul_comm, mul_left_comm]
  ring

-- Helper: Verification that (3, 11) works
lemma sq_3_11 : ∃ m : ℕ, 3^2 + 7*3*11 + 11^2 = m^2 := by
  use 38
  norm_num

-- Helper: Verification that (11, 3) works  
lemma sq_11_3 : ∃ m : ℕ, 11^2 + 7*11*3 + 3^2 = m^2 := by
  use 38
  norm_num

-- Helper: Forward direction - if there exists an m, then we must have one of the three cases
lemma forward_implies_cases (p q : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hq : Nat.Prime q)
    (h : ∃ m : ℕ, p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 = m^2) :
    p = q ∨ (p = 3 ∧ q = 11) ∨ (p = 11 ∧ q = 3) := by
  sorry

-- Helper: Backward direction - each of the three cases produces a square
lemma backward_cases_imply_square (p q : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hq : Nat.Prime q) :
    p = q ∨ (p = 3 ∧ q = 11) ∨ (p = 11 ∧ q = 3) → 
    ∃ m : ℕ, p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 = m^2 := by
  sorry

-- Main theorem statement as given in the problem
theorem rmo_2001_2 (p q : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hq : Nat.Prime q) :
  (∃ m : ℕ, p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 = m^2) ↔
    (p = q ∨ (p = 3 ∧ q = 11) ∨ (p = 11 ∧ q = 3)) := by
  apply And.intro
  · -- Forward direction
    intro h
    exact forward_implies_cases p q hp hq h
  · -- Backward direction
    intro h
    exact backward_cases_imply_square p q hp hq h
```

```lean
lemma bound_between_squares (p q : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hq : Nat.Prime q)

  (p + 3*q)^2 < p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 ∧ p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 < (p + 4*q)^2 := by sorry

lemma bound_between_squares_sym (p q : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hq : Nat.Prime q)

  (q + 3*p)^2 < q^2 + 7*p*q + p^2 ∧ q^2 + 7*p*q + p^2 < (q + 4*p)^2 := by sorry
```
